verdicts.trueWording: Small value was placed on preserving a "true" text
verdicts.note: Raw sfsfss.com transcription fetched (200, 95KB). Quote appears word for word in the compiler's headnote paragraph introducing Sem Gridji's story ('The following is a short story...'), which generalises about Seggri's classical poems and plays. The framing voice explicitly calls itself a report earlier ('As of the date of this report'), so the 'inside the report' limb holds; the construction is indeed agentless past passive. Caveat: fan transcription, not an authoritative edition.

verdicts.trueWording: was damaged in transit, and the rest of the third chapter
verdicts.note: loa.org fetched raw (200). In the final Q&A (the Dangerous People question), Attebery quotes the book: the copy Pandora sent from the Valley was damaged in transit and the closing pages are lost. Page earlier identifies Pandora as Le Guin's narrative stand-in and mentions 'Pandora's notes on the story', supporting the 'editorial note' limb; the flat catalogue-entry manner is observable in the quoted sentence itself.

verdicts.trueWording: the last ten or twenty pages of the novel, are lost
verdicts.note: Same loa.org fetch, same final answer, same quoted note. The extent is given as the hedged range 'ten or twenty' rather than an exact figure, exactly as claimed.

verdicts.trueWording: you can start with "The Back of the Book" and relish
verdicts.note: loa.org, the answer to the Delany/how-to-approach question (fourth Q&A). Full sentence offers it as one entry route and names 'the intricate world-building'. The 'rather than as an appendix' limb is carried by the surrounding framing (a hypertext without the electronic interface; readers invited to find their own ways through); the page never uses the word appendix.

verdicts.trueWording: are here the core of the text
verdicts.note: reactormag.com fetched raw (200); byline 'By Matthew Keeley', published March 15, 2019. Paragraph beginning 'The table of contents' says the scholarly materials, culture notes and literary excerpts that might comprise the Appendices to doorstop fantasy novels are here the core of the text. Every limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: This is a book that aspires to placehood.
verdicts.note: Same Reactor page. The sentence closes the paragraph that opens 'A warning: If you read solely for plot...' and contains 'This novel represents a culmination'; the claim's locator points mid-paragraph, but the wording is verbatim and 'aspires to placehood' is exactly ambition to become a place.

verdicts.trueWording: this novel is presented as a report from Genly Ai
verdicts.note: PDF fetched (200, 576KB, 44 pages) and text extracted with pypdf. Header confirms 'CSU EXPOSITORY READING AND WRITING COURSE | SEMESTER TWO / STUDENT VERSION', module The Left Hand of Darkness. The sentence continues 'to an Eku-men official on another planet', supporting the addressee limb. Locator nit: the passage sits in Activity 12 (Continued) on printed page 72, not 73.

verdicts.trueWording: It is called an ansible document.
verdicts.note: Same extracted PDF page (printed 72, Activity 12 Continued): the sentence directly follows the report-from-Genly-Ai sentence and names the in-world genre, then glosses the ansible as a faster-than-light communication device.

verdicts.trueWording: that's what's going to carry the reader
verdicts.note: Wayback raw id_ capture of the Paris Review interview fetched (200, full closing text present). Closing exchange on rhythm: even if the rhythm is very complicated and subtle, that is what carries the reader. All limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: Because they know they haven't got time
verdicts.note: Same capture, final answer. Preceding sentence: she thinks about old painters, who get so simple in their means, then 'Just so plain and simple.' The admiring frame (late Beethoven as her model, 'you really need less') supports 'praises'. Quotation appears word for word.
Same final answer: minimalism is described as a highly self-conscious mannerist style she can't write and doesn't want to, set against her own 'you really need less'. Every limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: I found a less formal vocabulary and a cadence better suited
verdicts.note: Same capture, the answer following the interviewer's 'shift toward economy' question. The clause opens 'As I began to depart from the heroic or adventure tradition of fantasy' and closes 'to what I had to say'. Verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: I've eased up on the formality of the prose
verdicts.note: Same answer, first sentences: she notes a very long career, then this; she adds she likes a more colloquial voice now. The career-long framing is on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: still based largely on the styles of writers of earlier generations
verdicts.note: Claim carries no quote, so verbatim grading does not apply; the page states it plainly. Same 'shift toward economy' answer: in the sixties and seventies the language of serious fantasy rested on earlier generations' styles, naming Tolkien, then Dunsany, Eddison, MacDonald, back to Malory. All five names and the decades are present.

verdicts.trueWording: your language gets like your shoes or your kitchen gear
verdicts.note: Same answer: 'you get old and your language gets like your shoes or your kitchen gear' followed by no longer needing fancy stuff. Quotation word for word; both limbs (aging writer, no fancy stuff) supported.
